## Historical audit: H0182

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/hint-codex-experiments/runs/codex_parallel_12/lanes/codex_parallel_12_lane3/codex_parallel_12_lane3_H_r1/infer_logs/kea-atomic-signal-selectors/turn_1/trajs.json` (all event citations below refer to this file). This is a software task, not a scene task.

| Question | Evidence and finding |
|---|---|
| Goal | The student stated an intention to inspect the selector lifecycle, reproduce behavior, and implement and verify an opt-in engine (main agent event 1). The task name suggests atomic signal selectors, but the original task specification is not visible; exact requirements are unknown. |
| Autonomous exploration | The student inspected repository status and branches, package configuration, selectors, context, reducers, build and mount lifecycle, types, and React hooks (events 2–27). Existing selectors use `createSelector`; React hooks subscribe to the store (events 10 and 27). These are observations of existing code, not a demonstrated diagnosis or fix. |
| Blocker and changes | Git inspection showed a detached HEAD and `master`; explicit checks reported neither local `main` nor `origin/main`, and identified `master` at `6c7ebba` (events 3, 11, 20). The student asked whether to branch from `master` or another `main` reference and said no branch or changes had been made (event 28). No edit or test execution appears in the trace. |
| Validation and outcome | Inventory metadata reports a **zero-byte patch**, formally not solved, with 0/12 fail-to-pass and 139/139 pass-to-pass tests. Those are reported evaluation results, not evidence of a successful implementation or of tests run by the student. The session ended normally with a clarification question, rather than a visible technical interruption (top-level metadata, characters [0,4711); event 28). No algorithm was implemented, so an algorithmic failure cannot be established. |
| Teacher input | The inventory lists available hint and review files, but their contents and the actual system prompt are not included here. Availability does not establish receipt; the after-round review cannot have been input to this round. No delivered teacher instruction or adoption is visible in the events. |

**Lessons and uncertainty.** Transferably, checking repository references exposed a concrete setup ambiguity before modification. Task-specifically, the student explored selector construction and lifecycle, but did not reproduce or validate the requested behavior. It remains unknown whether the missing `main` reference truly prevented authorized work, what branch instructions the student received, what any teacher advised, or whether clarification would have led to a solution.
